Sam —

Great questions. I pulled together a compact cutover checklist and code snippets you can drop into your repo. Attached: redwood-sdk-samples.zip (Node + Python examples) and a short MPA (maintenance plan) PDF. TL;DR below, then the detailed snippets.

High level cutover approach
- Pre-cutover (2 weeks out): smoke test with short-lived sandbox API key, run 1000 synthetic requests with expected seq lengths.
- Staging (3 days out): full traffic replay at 10% concurrency to validate streaming and KV cache behavior.
- Cutover window: DNS switch + traffic split (80/20) for first 30 minutes, fallback policy to previous endpoint for 3 minutes on any 5xx spike.
- Post-cutover: 24h elevated monitoring + token-level latency/cost checks.

Token rotation / KMS notes
- Redwood supports short-lived JWTs issued by your KMS. We recommend token lifetime = 1h and automatic refresh on 401.
- For on-prem secrets, rotate every 7 days and audit via the Console.

Rate limit & retries (summary)
- Client-side concurrency cap: 8 concurrent POSTs to generation endpoint per instance.
- 429 handling: immediate jittered retry with exponential backoff starting 300ms (300ms, 700ms, 1.6s) up to 4 attempts, then fallback to queueing or degrade to cached response.
- 5xx handling: fast failover to secondary region/endpoint and alert.

Example Node snippet (simplified)
const fetchWithRetry = async (url, opts) => {
  let attempt = 0;
  while (attempt < 4) {
    try {
      const res = await fetch(url, opts);
      if (res.status === 429) throw { code: 429 };
      if (res.status >= 500) throw { code: res.status };
      return res.json();
    } catch (err) {
      attempt++;
      const backoff = Math.round(300 * Math.pow(2, attempt - 1) * (1 + Math.random() * 0.3));
      if (attempt >= 4) throw err;
      await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, backoff));
    }
  }
};

Streaming note: use Redwood's streaming clients in sdk-samples; do not hold long-lived socket per user — multiplex streams where possible.

I'll follow up with a proposed mutual action plan and timeline once you confirm Feb 15–18 is still the target.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sam — quick answers and a concise failover snippet from the runtime side.

1) Token refresh: If you control KMS, app-side refresh is preferred. Redwood accepts short-lived tokens (we validate at handshake). Recommended flow: app obtains signed JWT from your KMS @ TTL=1h, presents it in Authorization header. On 401 we return WWW-Authenticate with reason; client should fetch new token and retry once.

2) Traffic split: We support header-based routing for canarying (X-Redwood-Canary: true) and percentage-based split at the Edge. In the staged cutover we recommend:
- Phase A: Header canary (1% of users / test cohort) for 24h.
- Phase B: 80/20 split by edge for 30m, monitor token-level latency.
If you want per-user pinning, include a deterministic hash header (X-Redwood-UserHash).

3) Burst handling: If brief internal jobs produce bursts, client-side throttling + server-side burst credits are safest. We can provision a temporary burst allowance for your account (contact Ben for procurement), but you should also cap simultaneous active streams per instance (8) and backpressure the job.

Failover example (pseudo-JS):
async function callWithFailover(primaryUrl, secondaryUrl, opts) {
  try {
    return await fetchWithRetry(primaryUrl, opts); // from Aditya's snippet
  } catch (err) {
    if (err.code && (err.code === 429 || err.code >= 500)) {
      // quick secondary attempt, no retries — keep fallthrough slim to reduce latency
      try {
        return await fetchWithRetry(secondaryUrl, opts);
      } catch (err2) {
        // escalate: emit metrics + alert, then bubble up
        emitMetric('integration.failover.attempt', 1);
        throw err2;
      }
    }
    throw err;
  }
}

Operational tips: emit per-request tags (route, model, token-id) so our Console can show token-level latency; set an SLO at 95th pct to detect regressions.

I'll sync with Ben to add the procurement/burst allowance notes.

—Vivek
Director, Customer Success Engineering, Redwood Inference
